It was already popular early on in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain, and it is still used there today. In the Basque Country it gained momentum and prestige in the last century, above all in the final years of the Franco regime, and became a marker of Basque identity and folk culture; new pipe-and-drum schools were set up, and together with the drum it provides the musical background for traditional dance ensembles. In Andalusia it is used in celebrations, the May Cross, sword dances and religious pilgrimages. Tuning also varies from place to place: the Basque Country and Andalusia commonly use whole tone, semitone, whole tone; Provence whole tone, whole tone, whole tone; and Britain whole tone, whole tone, semitone, corresponding to the lowest three holes of the tin whistle.

The galoubet, also called the three-hole pipe or tambourin pipe, is an aerophone with a mainly three-hole construction, designed to be blown with one hand while the other strikes a tabor drum, a bell, a psalterium, a tambourin à cordes, clappers or a triangle. Its origin is unknown, but it goes back at least to the twelfth century, and it was early on popular in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain, where it is still in use. In the Basque Country its standing rose over the last century, and especially in the final years of the Franco regime it became a marker of Basque identity and folk culture, providing the musical background for traditional dance ensembles; in Andalusia it is used for celebrations, the May Cross festival, sword dances and pilgrimage processions.
加羅笛屬氣鳴樂器，常以單手持笛，另一手敲擊塔博鼓、鐘、詩篇琴、弦鼓、骨板或三角鐵: The galoubet is an aerophone, usually held in one hand while the other strikes percussion such as a tabor drum, a bell, a psaltery, a string drum, bone clappers or a triangle. It has long been found in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain, and in the Basque Country it has become the pipe-and-drum accompaniment of traditional dance troupes; it also appears at festivals, the May Cross festival, sword dances and pilgrimage processions in Andalusia, and in the music associated with El Rocío in the province of Huelva this pipe is also called the pilgrimage pipe, the pilgrimage bagpipe or the soprano whistle.
加羅笛是一種古老的法國管樂器，音色明亮清脆，具有穿透力強的特質。其音域偏高，在中: The galoubet is an old French wind instrument with a bright, crisp timbre that carries well. Its range sits high, and it is especially strong in the middle-high register, where it produces a clear, lively sound. The instrument sounds through a single or double reed: the airflow sets the reed vibrating and the pipe resonates to amplify the volume. Its timbre is warm without losing lightness, somewhere between the modern clarinet and the traditional recorder, with a distinctive folk character. Compared with the heaviness of the saxophone it seems nimbler and more transparent; compared with the flute it has more of a warm wooden quality. Its sound projects well, which suits chamber music and folk performance where a melodic line has to stand out.
